name: Keir Pierce
life: “I still remember my own uniform left to dry over the shop till.” Monday often includes a stop at Maré Coffee, where Keir likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I caused the leak moving a hose to mop the floor. I reopened the shop on my evening off.
appearance: Keir is easy to recognize by thick, tightly coiled hair and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in a cropped bottle-green coat with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Keir looks down for a moment before saying something difficult when listening.
personality: Keir can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Keir can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To cover an evening wash shift to undo the damage.
family: Lena Osborne is Keir’s half-sibling. Keir chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Lena brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The upstairs piano*, Lena says, “I bought it so my son would come home to practice.”
connections: Rae Vargas. The repair shift is ordered by the bus schedule the pupils worked out for the iron. Also in the story is Dale Valdez (school contact).

reactions.response: Keir asks the children and families whether they want to appear in the picture.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Keir brings the envelope to the counter unopened and stays long enough to make a note of who accepted it.
